metadata.case_name: LEE YU HEY v. YUEN HIS CARL

plaintiff.occupation_after: self-employed driver; later employed as driver (since July 2012) earning $13,000 monthly

injuries.description: Prolapsed intervertebral disc at L5/S1 level
source: Dr Lau diagnosed the plaintiff as suffering from “Sprained soft tissue injury of back region, with prolapsed disc of L5/S1 level”.
MRI of the lumbar spine showed protrusion of the intervertebral disc at the L5S1 level.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the abdomen, lower back, lumbar spine or pelvis

injuries.description: Broad based posterior disc bulge at L4/5 level
source: On 23 April 2009, MRI was conducted on the plaintiff’s lumbar spine. It showed “[b]road based posterior disc bulge is seen at L4/5 level… Small anterior marginal osteophytes and anterior disc bulges are seen at L4/5 and L5/S1 levels”.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the abdomen, lower back, lumbar spine or pelvis

injuries.description: Sprained soft tissue injury of back region
source: Dr Lau diagnosed the plaintiff as suffering from “Sprained soft tissue injury of back region, with prolapsed disc of L5/S1 level”.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of lumbar spine

manifestations.description: low back pain with radiation to right leg
mild decrease in right leg sensation
pain over lumbosacral spine with decreased motion range of the back
straight leg raising test on the right side was limited (SLR right about 45-50 degrees with pain)
mild weakness of the right great toe motion
reported walking tolerance was about 3 to 4 minutes
Range of motion (ROM) of lumbar spine: flexion: touch knee back pain; extension: 20 degree with leg pain (first course) and subsequent ROM limitations described in physiotherapy reports

treatments_received.treatment: physiotherapy (3 courses, 28 sessions in total) at Alice Ho Miu Ling Nethersole Hospital
source: Between 8 December 2008 and 2 February 2010, the plaintiff attended 3 courses of physiotherapy (28 sessions in total) at AHMLNH. The physiotherapists’ report dated 30 November 2010 includes these findings: “Range of motion (ROM) of lumbar spine: flexion: touch knee back pain: extension: 20 degree with leg pain” (1st Course Physiotherapy) … “Straight leg raising (SLR): right 50 degrees with pain, left 70 degrees without pain… His reported walking tolerance was about 3 to 4 minutes.” (Final Clinical Findings)

treatments_received.treatment: discectomy of the L5S1 intervertebral disc (surgical)
source: There was persistent symptom after the physiotherapy. MRI of the lumbar spine showed protrusion of the intervertebral disc at the L5S1 level. Since his activities of daily living was very much affected, he was admitted on 21 Sept 2009 for discectomy of the L5S1 intervertebral disc on 22 Sept 2009…

treatments_received.treatment: treatment by Chinese bonesetter (6 sessions between 9 and 14 March 2009)
source: As evidenced by various receipts, the plaintiff attended 6 sessions of treatment from a Chinese bonesetter between 9 and 14 March 2009.

treatments_received.treatment: acupuncture (2 sessions at HKU SPACE Chinese Medicine Clinics and Pharmacies on 18 and 19 March 2009)
source: He also attended 2 sessions by acupuncturists of HKU SPACE Chinese Medicine Clinics and Pharmacies on 18 and 19 March 2009

treatments_received.treatment: further Chinese medical practitioner treatments (5 sessions between 21 March and 9 April 2009)
source: and another 5 treatment sessions by another Chinese medical practitioner between 21 March and 9 April 2009.

losses.description: Residual back pain and stiffness as a result of the injury in the Accident.
Reduced walking tolerance (reported walking tolerance was about 3 to 4 minutes) and limited straight leg raising on the right with pain.
